summary.text: The candidates with the strongest convergent evidence are hypoxia-programme surface or metabolic proteins made by the tumour cells themselves. CA9 leads the overall convergence ranking: it is strongly induced in tumour RNA [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312], the change grows when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787], tumour cells carry nearly all its transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and literature and clinical antibodies support it. NNMT and SLC16A3 add protein that replicates in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776] [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551], and CD70 combines tumour up-regulation with clinical antibody programmes.

The best biomarkers are mostly genes lost from the proximal-tubule cell of origin, and they carry prognostic information that the targets lack. PSAT1 tops the biomarker profile: its protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946] and its residual expression within tumours goes with worse survival in TCGA-KIRC [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.43]. ALDH6A1 is the mirror image, a dosage-sensitive loss whose retention goes with better survival [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554], and ALDOB and PCK1 mark loss of tubule identity. NNMT is the one candidate that is both a convincing target and an adverse prognostic biomarker [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301].

Several high-ranked genes weaken under the independent layers. SCARB1, first in the target profile, is shared between tumour cells and macrophages [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.384], its attribution changes between single-cell datasets and its protein is enriched in adrenal gland [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08]. HK2 does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256]. KDR, the drugged anti-angiogenic target, is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and no leading candidate is a selective DepMap dependency of ccRCC lines.

Beyond the well-known genes, the discovery screen identified two unexplored tumour-cell candidates and prioritised them for experimental validation. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made by tumour cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], a call that holds in a second single-cell dataset [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.941]; its increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.829], survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], is confirmed at protein level in CPTAC and gives a strong conjugate-suitability score [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.705]. What is missing is proof that the protein sits on the tumour-cell surface (mass-spectrometry surfaceome has not seen it), normal-tissue staining, any dependency, confirmatory-cohort data and homogeneity, since few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.5%]. RAB42, an intracellular small GTPase, is also tumour-cell made, replicated in TCGA-KIRC [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and purity-robust, but is not antibody-accessible and has no dependency or confirmatory data. Immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal-tissue arrays, surface flow cytometry and knockout studies in three-dimensional or organoid models would test both; the best immune-track gene, MILR1, is a macrophage receptor whose signal vanishes in a pure tumour, and the stroma track is led by the fibroblast protein OLFML2A. Here novel means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and nothing shows that targeting these genes would help patients.

Translational layers temper all calls. No gene separates the arms of IMmotion150 or the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial after correction; CD70 is only associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383] without significance [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166]. CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup candidate [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148], and CD70 has one of the best conjugate profiles [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746] while CA9 carries an off-tumour stomach signal.

omics.text: Up-regulated, protein-confirmed and purity-robust products define the target side. CA9 protein rises in paired tumours [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]; NDUFA4L2 (COXFA4L2) has the largest protein increase among the leaders [gene=COXFA4L2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=3.768]; CD70 [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421], NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709] and SLC16A3 [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.279] follow. For SLC16A3 the phosphosite increase disappears after adjusting for protein [gene=SLC16A3; type=phosphosite_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; protein_adjusted_log2fc=-0.607], so it reflects abundance rather than signalling.

Strongly down-regulated genes mark loss of tubule identity and are biomarkers, not targets: PSAT1 RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.867] and protein [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963], and PCK1 protein [gene=PCK1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.859]. The mechanism is the loss of chromosome arm three-p: VHL is lost in most tumours [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791] and mutated in about half [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483], while PBRM1 loss lowers its own RNA [gene=PBRM1; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; rna_rho=0.714]. Protein-adjusted kinase activity points to mTOR signalling through RPS6KB1 [gene=RPS6KB1; type=kinase_activity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; ksea_z=3.289].

literature.text: Literature and data converge on CA9, CD70 and NNMT. CA9 is described as enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low normal-kidney background and as a PET imaging target that still needs prospective validation (PMID 42473996); CD70 as overexpressed in RCC, minimally expressed in normal tissue and a target of single-domain antibody radiotracers (PMID 38195301, PMID 39510586); NNMT as an upregulated, adverse-prognosis gene with a single supporting study (PMID 41399267) and potent research inhibitors (PMID 37523719). NDUFA4L2 is linked to proliferation, HIF-driven induction and ferroptosis suppression (PMID 36722045, PMID 42331208), and SLC16A3 to lactate-driven immune evasion in one study (PMID 42028950).

The literature is thin where the data are strongest for biomarkers. PSAT1, first in the biomarker profile, appears only in a bioinformatic enrichment sentence (PMID 41971124), and PPP1R1A, whose loss replicates strongly in TCGA-KIRC [gene=PPP1R1A; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-5.179], has no literature relation in the corpus. Conversely, ALDOB is proposed as an immunotherapy target on the basis of infiltration correlations that the data do not support, since it is a lost tubule enzyme (PMID 40852386).

external.text: Open Targets separates genetic drivers from druggable effectors. VHL is the top ccRCC association [gene=VHL; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6466] but is not druggable; EPAS1 is strongly associated [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871] and has the approved inhibitor BELZUTIFAN; KDR has many approved anti-angiogenic drugs. Among the convergence leaders, CA9 has clinical antibodies including GIRENTUXIMAB, CD70 has CUSATUZUMAB (PHASE_2) and conjugates, ENPP3 has the conjugate AGS-16C3F (PHASE_2), while SCARB1, NNMT and SLC16A3 are tractable but untested in the clinic.

Druggability is not matched by dependency. NNMT is not a dependency of ccRCC lines [gene=NNMT; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.316]; CCND1 is essential [gene=CCND1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-1.229] but not selectively so [gene=CCND1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.36]; and even EPAS1 only trends towards selective dependence [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.061], reflecting that two-dimensional lines miss HIF-2 biology.

cells.text: Single-cell data split the candidates into tumour-intrinsic and microenvironment genes. CA9 is tumour-intrinsic, with about half of tumour cells expressing it [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=54.7%]. KDR is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], CD74 is carried mainly by macrophages [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436] and CXCR4 by lymphocytes [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD4_T; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=87.8%]: these are microenvironment targets. EPAS1 transcripts are spread across cell types, with endothelium holding the largest share [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365].

Two bulk-omics leaders are not cleanly tumour-intrinsic. SCARB1 transcripts are split between tumour cells [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.336] and macrophages, with endothelium the highest per cell [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; cpm_share=0.406]. CD70 is attributed mainly to T/NK cells in Li 2022 [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.345] but to tumour cells in Zhang 2021 [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.964]. FCER1G bulk up-regulation is infiltration, as its expression falls with purity [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692].

spatial.text: In Visium sections CA9 spot expression is explained by tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; composition_corrected_share=0.999] and its high spots are surrounded by tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381], with only a slight macrophage enrichment. KDR spot expression is attributed to endothelium [gene=KDR; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=Endothelial; composition_corrected_share=0.99] in a vascular niche that also borders tumour cells, consistent with its role as a stromal target.

structure.text: Structural-context scores are descriptive heuristics of predicted monomers, not evidence of a degron or degrader. The CA9 model has moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56], its top cavity is small [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] and detected cavities recover half of the experimental ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5], which validates cavity detection only. KDR scores among the highest [gene=KDR; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.841] at its kinase-domain cavity, but it is endothelial. No curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference was used for these candidates.

discovery.text: COL23A1 is a transmembrane collagen and the leading tumour-track candidate. Tumour cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. The increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.829] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It is not prognostic [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.123] and is not a DepMap dependency. What is missing is cell-surface confirmation by mass spectrometry, normal-tissue staining, functional evidence and confirmatory-cohort data, so it is a data-ranked hypothesis prioritised for validation.

RAB42 is a little-studied small GTPase made mostly by tumour cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. Its rise replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and holds in a pure tumour [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189]. It is intracellular, so an antibody cannot reach it, it is neither prognostic nor a dependency, and it was not measured in the confirmatory cohort; a small-molecule or degrader route would need functional proof first.

In the stroma track OLFML2A, a secreted matrix protein, is made mostly by fibroblasts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]. Its increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=OLFML2A; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.372] and persists in a pure tumour [gene=OLFML2A; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527]. It is not a dependency and has no confirmatory-cohort data.

The immune track, which holds most of the discovery pool, is led by MILR1, a macrophage receptor with no ccRCC papers. Macrophages make most of its transcripts [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.841]. Its increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=MILR1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.436] and goes with worse survival [gene=MILR1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.343]. However it nearly vanishes in a pure tumour [gene=MILR1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], so it reflects myeloid infiltration and would be a microenvironment, not a tumour-cell, target.

validation.text: External replication and the confirmatory cohort strengthen NNMT, SLC16A3 and PSAT1. NNMT replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.685] and in confirmatory proteomics [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]; SLC16A3 protein and its shared phosphosite replicate [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551]; and PSAT1 protein loss replicates [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. HK2 is weakened: its protein change does not replicate [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256] and is not significant there [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074]. CA9 and COL23A1 were not tested in the confirmatory cohort, which is missing data rather than failure.

Driver status, dependency and purity sort the rest. Only the arm-loss and chromatin genes are recurrent drivers, led by VHL [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483] and PBRM1 [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362]; none of the expression leaders is mutated. No candidate is a selective DepMap dependency: SCD is a borderline, non-selective dependency [gene=SCD; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-0.501]. The purity check supports CA9 [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787] and exposes FCER1G as infiltration [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692]. Protein-adjusted kinase activity highlights RPS6KB1 [gene=RPS6KB1; type=kinase_activity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; ksea_z=3.289], consistent with mTOR signalling.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, the top of the target profile is stable: SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, FABP6 and CYP2J2 stay in the top ten in most perturbations and their rank intervals are narrow. In the biomarker profile PSAT1 is the most robust, followed by PCK1, SLC6A19 and ALDH6A1. The overall convergence ranking is more weight-dependent: CA9 and NDUFA4L2 stay near the top, but NDUFA4L2 falls far in the target profile because it lacks predicted tractability, and many convergence leaders such as ALDOB, UMOD and NPHS2 rank highly only through literature and loss-of-tubule signals.

Weight-dependent candidates include HK2, ANGPTL4 and the lower half of the target top twenty-five, whose intervals extend far beyond the top ten, and biomarkers such as DUSP9, L1CAM and SLPI that leave the top twenty-five when a single stream such as omics or prognosis is removed. These should be read as secondary candidates whose position depends on the chosen weights.

treatment.text: IMmotion150 and the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial show associations only: no gene separates the combination from sunitinib, or nivolumab from everolimus, after correction. Higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383] without significance [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166] and without a between-arm difference [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.934]. Higher CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], again not significant [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332], and NNMT shows nothing on nivolumab [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.padj=0.88].

subtypes.text: CA9 is the clearest subgroup candidate: higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in CPTAC RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971] and TCGA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148], and lower in ccB tumours [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-1.551]. PSAT1 rises with BAP1 mutation in TCGA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] and in the aggressive ccB subtype [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364], whereas SLC16A3 does not change with PBRM1 at protein level [gene=SLC16A3; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.631]. Differences in immune genes between subgroups may reflect infiltration rather than tumour-cell expression.

adc.text: CD70 has one of the best conjugate profiles [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], with surface topology and no vital-organ protein enrichment, but it is heterogeneous across donors [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%] and lacks staining data. The controls behave as expected: CA9 scores well [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647] but is enriched in stomach [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19], and ENPP3 is held back by kidney and duodenum staining [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578].

Among new candidates, COL23A1 ranks near the top for conjugates [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.705] but few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.5%]. SCARB1 is a poor conjugate target given adrenal enrichment [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08] and low homogeneity [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%]. A high score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: MILR1 and LILRB4 are immune-cell genes that mark hot, myeloid-rich tumours. MILR1 transcripts come almost only from immune cells [gene=MILR1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.995] and track M2 macrophages [gene=MILR1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_m2_macrophages=0.586]; LILRB4 follows the overall immune score [gene=LILRB4; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.853]. The checkpoint control PDCD1 tracks CD8 T cells [gene=PDCD1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.811]. CD70 sits in between, with a large immune share of its transcripts [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], so its tumour-cell attribution needs protein-level confirmation.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9 (tumour-intrinsic, purity-robust, literature-backed, clinical antibodies), CD70 (surface, clinical antibodies, best conjugate profile, but uncertain cell attribution) and NNMT (replicated in two cohorts, prognostic, chemical matter but no clinical drug). They disagree on SCARB1, ranked first by data and genetics but mixed in cell source and enriched in adrenal gland; on ALDOB, a literature favourite that the data treat as a lost-tubule biomarker; and on PSAT1, the strongest data biomarker with almost no literature. EPAS1 and KDR remain the validated mechanism and microenvironment targets, while VHL and PBRM1 explain the disease without being druggable.

targets.rationale: First in overall convergence and second in the target profile with a narrow interval; tumour-intrinsic and purity-robust, literature and clinical antibodies; limitations are stomach protein enrichment and no confirmatory-cohort data.

Surface antigen up in RNA and protein, best conjugate profile among known targets and clinical antibodies; ranked below CA9 because its cell attribution differs between single-cell datasets and expression is heterogeneous.
Up-regulated, purity-robust, replicated in TCGA-KIRC and the confirmatory cohort and adverse-prognostic, with research inhibitors; intracellular enzyme with no clinical drug and no DepMap dependency.
Plasma-membrane lactate exporter, up at protein level and replicated in the confirmatory cohort, pan-subtype and robust in the target profile; no clinical drug and no dependency.
Most robust biomarker-profile gene: protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, adverse prognosis in TCGA-KIRC and higher in ccB and BAP1-mutant tumours; little literature.
Validated mechanism target with approved belzutifan; placed below the data leaders because bulk RNA and cell-line data cannot capture HIF-2 protein biology.
Largest protein increase and second in overall convergence, with strong literature on HIF-driven induction and ferroptosis; intracellular with no specific drug, so it falls in the target profile.
Dosage-sensitive loss with favourable-prognosis association in TCGA-KIRC; a tubule-metabolism biomarker, not a target.
Known conjugate target with confirmed surface protein and a clinical conjugate; moderate suitability because of normal kidney and duodenum staining.
First in the target profile, but ranked lower here because its transcripts are shared with macrophages, the attribution differs between datasets and its protein is enriched in adrenal gland.
High in overall convergence through literature and a strong loss in tumours; a lost-tubule prognostic biomarker, not an immunotherapy target as some papers propose.

Exploratory: tumour-cell transmembrane collagen, replicated in TCGA-KIRC and a second single-cell dataset, purity-robust and a strong conjugate score; main limitation is unconfirmed surface protein, missing normal-tissue staining and no dependency or confirmatory data.
Exploratory: tumour-cell GTPase replicated in TCGA-KIRC and purity-robust; main limitation is that it is intracellular, so not antibody-accessible, with no functional or confirmatory evidence.

limitations.text: This is the single-agent arm of an architecture benchmark: one analyst covered the five specialist scopes with fewer tool calls per layer than the multi-agent version.
Treatment-response results are single-gene associations from small trial arms; no gene separates the arms after correction.
No candidate is a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap, and two-dimensional cell lines miss HIF-2 biology.
Single-cell attribution of CD70 and SCARB1 differs between datasets; CA9, COL23A1, RAB42 and OLFML2A were not tested in the confirmatory cohort.
Literature support is limited to the ingested abstract corpus, and discovery novelty is counted by gene-symbol literature volume.
Structural-context scores describe predicted monomer cavities and do not identify degrons or predict degradation.
Passing the automatic checks means no failures were detected, not complete scientific validation.
